chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir and from Fadalah from al-Ala' from Muhammad, all from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about a man who made a will bequeathing something to another man, and the beneficiary died before the testator. He said: 'It is nothing (void).'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a will if the beneficiary dies before the testator?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a bequest (*wasiyyah*) is contingent upon the beneficiary's survival at the moment of the testator's death; if the beneficiary predeceases the testator, the bequest lapses entirely. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the right to the bequest is not merely a potential claim but a vested right that must exist at the time of death, distinguishing it from inheritance which may pass to heirs. The concise ruling ('laysa bi-shay') reflects the practical application of testamentary law in early Islamic society, ensuring clarity in estate distribution.
